policy_title: Reduce A&E waiting times with 'Pharmacy First' and tax incentives
stated: Reform UK will cut A&E waiting times through a 'Pharmacy First, GP Second, A&E Last' campaign, and offer tax incentives for new pharmacies and those employing more staff.

source.quote: Save A&E Cut waiting times with a campaign of ‘Pharmacy First, GP Second, A&E Last’. We will offer tax incentives for new pharmacies and those who employ more staff to assist in relieving pressure on A&E.

bearing_set.reason: Directly targets A&E waiting times and primary care access through pharmacy-led triage and capacity expansion, bearing materially on whether people can get treated when they need it.

Tax incentives for new pharmacies and additional staff represent forgone public revenue; the net fiscal effect (revenue cost vs potential NHS savings from reduced A&E demand) is a concrete, non-negligible bearing on public-finances sustainability.

membership_note: Two clear bearings: O3 is the designed target; O12 is the cross-outcome tradeoff via forgone tax revenue. The employment element of the tax incentive is too narrow a sectoral effect to materially move O4 or O13 indicators.
